title: Taper fade vs skin fade: which cut fits you?
description: Compare taper fades and skin fades, including appearance, maintenance and who each cut suits best.

content.heading: The quick difference
paragraphs: A taper concentrates the shortest blend around the temples and neckline. A skin fade continues the blend around the full sides and back, taking the shortest section down to skin.
Both can look clean and modern. The right option depends on how much contrast you want and how regularly you plan to visit your barber.

content.heading: Choose a taper for subtle structure
paragraphs: A taper is a good fit when you want the edges to feel fresh while keeping more fullness through the sides. It grows out gently, works well in professional settings and can be paired with most lengths and textures on top.

content.heading: Choose a skin fade for maximum contrast
paragraphs: A skin fade makes the blend a major part of the haircut. It can sharpen a textured crop, balance extra height on top or create a clean backdrop for curls. The close finish is more visible as it grows, so regular appointments help maintain the look.

content.heading: Still unsure?
paragraphs: Book the service that feels closest to your goal and bring a reference. At the consultation we can adjust the fade height and finish to suit your head shape, texture and routine.
